weakness.title: Improper Protection of Emergency Exits Against Unauthorized Entry
weakness.description: An emergency exit can be used to enter the facility, or an area within it, without authorization.

extended_description.applicability: Doors and openings intended for exit in an emergency, on the perimeter of the facility or of a protected area. Regular entrances are not affected.
extended_description.exploitation: An unauthorized person enters through an emergency exit because it can be opened from the outside, has been left open, or is not monitored.

row.details: Entry controls at regular entrances are bypassed.
Unauthorized persons reach information, media and equipment inside.
Equipment can be altered by persons who entered unseen.

row.description: Fit emergency exits with no external handle, key cylinder or other means of opening from the outside.
Fit each emergency exit with a door position sensor, and raise an alert when it opens outside an emergency.
Use self-closing doors and detect doors left open.
Check exits for tampering, devices that hold them open, and damaged hardware.
No protection may prevent or delay opening from the inside. Hardware must comply with the applicable fire and building regulations.
Delayed-egress locks and local alarms are acceptable only where regulations permit them.
Exits must not be blocked or locked against entry by chains, bars or similar means.

row.reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: PE-3 Physical Access Control, PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access
ISO/IEC 27001:2022, Annex A: 7.1 Physical security perimeters, 7.4 Physical security monitoring
